scenario: A user needs BitLocker and the ability to join a company domain. Which Windows edition is the minimum?

options.note: No BitLocker management or domain join.

explanation: Pro adds BitLocker, domain join, Group Policy Editor and Remote Desktop host.

scenario: Which hardware requirement must a PC meet to install Windows 11?
explanation: Windows 11 also needs a supported 64-bit CPU, 4 GB RAM and 64 GB storage.

scenario: Which command shows a Windows PC's IP address, DNS servers and MAC address?
explanation: ipconfig /release and /renew get a new DHCP lease; /flushdns clears the DNS cache.

scenario: Which command shows each router hop on the path to a destination?
explanation: On Linux and macOS the command is traceroute.

scenario: Which command tests DNS name resolution directly?
explanation: nslookup queries a DNS server for records.

scenario: Which command repairs corrupted Windows system files?
explanation: System File Checker replaces damaged protected files. DISM can repair the component store it uses.

scenario: Which command checks a drive for file system errors and bad sectors?
explanation: /f fixes errors; /r also locates bad sectors and recovers readable data.

scenario: Which command applies new Group Policy settings immediately?
explanation: gpresult shows which policies were applied to the user and computer.

scenario: Which command copies folders with options to mirror and retry, and is suited for large file copies?

options.note: Basic copy with verification; no mirroring.
Older copy tool; no mirror or retry options.

explanation: Robust File Copy supports mirroring, resume and logging.

scenario: Which tool shows running processes and CPU and memory use, and lets you end an unresponsive app?
explanation: Task Manager also manages startup apps and shows performance.

scenario: Which tool shows system, application and security logs to investigate errors?
explanation: Look for errors and warnings around the time of the problem.

scenario: A device shows a yellow exclamation mark. Which tool is this in, and what does it mean?

options.text: Device Manager; a driver or device problem
Event Viewer; a security log entry

explanation: Update, roll back or reinstall the driver.

scenario: Which tool creates, deletes and formats partitions with a graphical interface?
explanation: diskpart is the command-line equivalent.

scenario: Which tool is used to start, stop and set startup types for background services?
explanation: Startup types include Automatic, Automatic (Delayed), Manual and Disabled.

scenario: Which tool can start Windows in diagnostic or selective startup mode to troubleshoot?
explanation: Startup programs are managed in Task Manager in modern Windows.

scenario: Which file system should be used for a USB drive that must store files larger than 4 GB and work on Windows and macOS?
explanation: exFAT is designed for flash media across platforms.

scenario: Which Windows file system supports file permissions and encryption with EFS?
explanation: NTFS also supports compression, quotas and journaling.

scenario: Which partition style supports drives larger than 2 TB and is required for UEFI boot on Windows 11?

options.note: Limited to 2 TB and four primary partitions.
A file system, not a partition style.

explanation: GUID Partition Table supports many partitions and very large disks.

scenario: Which type of Windows installation keeps the user's files and apps while moving to a newer version?
explanation: A clean install starts fresh; back up data first.

scenario: Which macOS feature provides automatic backups to an external drive?

options.note: Cloud file sync, not local backups.

explanation: Time Machine keeps hourly, daily and weekly backups.

scenario: Which macOS feature encrypts the startup disk?
explanation: FileVault is similar to BitLocker on Windows.

scenario: Which macOS app stores passwords, certificates and secure notes?
explanation: iCloud Keychain can sync passwords across Apple devices.

scenario: Which Linux command shows the current working directory?
explanation: Other basics: ls, cd, cp, mv, rm, mkdir, cat, nano.

scenario: Which Linux command changes file permissions?
explanation: Example: chmod 755 script.sh gives the owner full rights and others read and execute.

scenario: Which Linux command runs a single command with administrator (root) privileges?
explanation: sudo uses your own password and logs the command.

scenario: Which command installs software on Ubuntu or Debian Linux?
explanation: Package managers download and install software from repositories.

scenario: Which Linux command searches text in files for a pattern?

options.note: Searches for files by name or attributes.

explanation: Example: grep error /var/log/syslog.

scenario: Which Windows tool lets you edit Group Policy on a single Pro computer?
explanation: Local Group Policy Editor isn't available in Home editions.

scenario: Which Control Panel or Settings area changes which app opens a file type?
explanation: Settings > Apps > Default apps controls file associations.

scenario: Which tool schedules a script to run every night at 2 AM on Windows?
explanation: Tasks can run on schedules or triggers like logon or events.

scenario: Which tool shows detailed information about hardware, drivers and system components?
explanation: dxdiag shows DirectX and display information.

scenario: Which Windows setting turns off automatic sleep when a laptop is plugged in?
explanation: Power plans control sleep, hibernate and lid close actions.

scenario: Which mobile OS lets users install apps from outside the official store (sideloading) more easily by default?

options.note: Restricted by default in most regions.

explanation: Sideloading apps from unknown sources increases malware risk.

scenario: Which command restarts a Windows computer immediately?
explanation: /r restarts, /s shuts down, /t sets a delay in seconds.

scenario: Which command maps a network share to a drive letter?
explanation: Example: net use Z: \\server\share.

scenario: A user gets an email claiming to be from their bank, asking them to click a link and log in. What is this?
explanation: Vishing uses phone calls; smishing uses text messages; whaling targets executives.

scenario: Someone follows an employee through a secure door without badging in. What is this?
explanation: Access control vestibules and security awareness training help prevent tailgating.

scenario: An attacker watches a user type their PIN at a coffee shop. What is this?
explanation: Privacy screen filters help prevent it.

scenario: An attacker sets up a Wi-Fi network named like the coffee shop's to capture traffic. What is this?
explanation: Use VPNs and verify networks before connecting.

scenario: Files are encrypted and a message demands payment for the key. What type of malware is this?
explanation: Offline backups are the best protection.

scenario: Which malware hides deep in the operating system and is very hard to detect or remove?
explanation: Rootkits may require boot-time scans or reinstalling the OS.

scenario: Which malware records everything a user types?
explanation: Keyloggers steal passwords and other sensitive data.

scenario: A free game a user installed secretly opened a backdoor for attackers. What type of malware is this?
explanation: Trojans pretend to be legitimate software.

scenario: A PC's CPU is at 100% constantly and the fan is loud, but nothing obvious is running. Which malware is likely?
explanation: Cryptominers use system resources to mine cryptocurrency.

scenario: What is the first step in CompTIA's best-practice malware removal process?
explanation: Steps: verify symptoms; quarantine; disable System Restore; remediate; schedule scans and updates; enable System Restore and create a restore point; educate the user.

scenario: Why should System Restore be disabled during malware removal?

options.text: Restore points may contain the malware

explanation: After cleaning, re-enable it and create a new clean restore point.

scenario: What should a technician do with an infected PC before cleaning it?

options.text: Share its files with other users

explanation: Disconnect it to prevent spreading.

scenario: Which is the most secure Wi-Fi security setting?
explanation: WPA3 and WPA2 use AES; avoid WEP and TKIP.

scenario: A company wants employees to authenticate to Wi-Fi with their own network credentials through a central server. What should be used?
explanation: Enterprise mode uses 802.1X with a RADIUS server.

scenario: Which is an example of multifactor authentication?

options.text: A security question and a PIN

explanation: Factors: something you know, something you have, something you are.

scenario: Which principle gives users only the permissions needed for their job?
explanation: Use standard accounts for daily work and admin rights only when needed.

scenario: Which Windows feature prompts before changes that need administrator rights?
explanation: UAC helps stop malware from silently making system changes.

scenario: Which Windows feature encrypts an entire drive?
explanation: BitLocker To Go encrypts removable drives.

scenario: A shared folder's share permission is Read, and the user's NTFS permission is Full Control. What access do they have over the network?
explanation: When share and NTFS permissions combine, the most restrictive applies.

scenario: Which built-in Windows tool provides antivirus and anti-malware protection?
explanation: Keep definitions updated and run scans regularly.

scenario: Which physical security control uses two doors so only one person can enter at a time?
explanation: Vestibules (formerly called mantraps) prevent tailgating.

scenario: Which data destruction method is best for an old hard drive that must never be read again?

options.text: Deleting files and emptying the trash

explanation: Degaussing works on magnetic drives, not SSDs. Get a certificate of destruction from vendors.

scenario: A company wants to reuse old drives internally while making old data unrecoverable. What should it do?

options.text: Run a quick format on each drive

explanation: Overwriting (wiping) or the drive's secure erase command make data unrecoverable while keeping the drive.

scenario: A website shows a certificate warning in the browser. What should the user do?

options.text: Not enter information and report it
Click through and log in quickly

explanation: Invalid or expired certificates can indicate interception or a fake site.

scenario: Which browser practice improves security?

options.text: Save passwords in a text file

explanation: Keep browsers updated and use a password manager.

scenario: A lost company phone contains sensitive email. What should the admin do first?

options.text: Remotely lock or wipe it with MDM
Wait to see if it's returned
Change the Wi-Fi password at home

explanation: Locator apps can help find it, but protect the data first.

scenario: Which mobile setting best protects a phone if it's stolen?
explanation: Combine screen locks with full-device encryption and remote wipe.

scenario: Which account type should be used for everyday work on a Windows PC?
explanation: Use admin accounts only for administrative tasks.

scenario: Which type of attack tries every possible password until one works?
explanation: Account lockout policies and long passwords defend against brute force.

scenario: Which Windows feature lets users sign in with a face, fingerprint or PIN tied to the device?
explanation: Windows Hello is a passwordless sign-in option.

scenario: Which protocol is used for network authentication in Active Directory domains?
explanation: Kerberos issues tickets so users don't send passwords repeatedly.

scenario: Which describes a zero-day vulnerability?

options.text: A flaw exploited before a patch exists
A bug fixed on the day it's found
A virus that runs at midnight
A patch released on day zero

explanation: Defense in depth and fast patching reduce the risk.

scenario: An employee gets a call from "IT support" asking for their password. What is this?
explanation: IT staff should never ask for passwords.

scenario: Which security measure locks an account after several failed sign-in attempts?
explanation: Lockout slows brute-force attacks.

scenario: Which is an example of something you HAVE as an authentication factor?
explanation: Smart cards and authenticator apps on phones are also possession factors.

scenario: A Windows PC shows a blue screen (BSOD) right after a new driver was installed. What should be tried first?

options.text: Use Safe Mode to roll back the driver

explanation: Safe Mode loads minimal drivers so you can remove the faulty one.

scenario: Windows is slow, and Task Manager shows memory usage near 100%. What helps most?

options.text: Close unneeded apps or add more RAM

explanation: Check for memory-hungry processes or malware.

scenario: A PC takes a long time to boot. Which tool helps disable unnecessary startup apps?
explanation: Disabling startup apps speeds boot and login.

scenario: An application crashes every time it opens. What should be tried first?

options.note: Checks system files, not the app.

explanation: Check Event Viewer for errors; try repair, update or reinstall.

scenario: A service needed by an app doesn't start at boot. Where should the technician look?
explanation: Check the startup type, dependencies and logon account.

scenario: A user's PC clock keeps drifting and Kerberos sign-in errors appear. What should be checked?
explanation: Kerberos requires clocks to be closely synchronized.

scenario: After a Windows update, a PC won't boot properly. Which option can undo recent system changes without affecting personal files?

options.text: Reset this PC with Remove everything

explanation: System Restore reverts system files, drivers and settings to an earlier point.

scenario: Which recovery option reinstalls Windows but can keep personal files?

options.text: Reset this PC with Keep my files

explanation: Apps are removed, so reinstall them afterward.

scenario: A user's profile takes a very long time to load at sign-in. What could help?
explanation: Corrupt profiles can be fixed by creating a new profile and migrating data.

scenario: A browser keeps redirecting to unwanted sites and showing pop-ups. What is the likely cause?

options.note: Possible, but pop-ups point to malware.

explanation: Remove unknown extensions, reset the browser and scan for malware.

scenario: A user receives security alerts from an antivirus they never installed, asking them to pay. What is this?
explanation: This is a common scam; follow the malware removal process.

scenario: Files have been renamed with strange extensions and can't be opened. What should be suspected?
explanation: Isolate the device immediately and restore from clean backups.

scenario: A phone's battery drains fast and data usage is unusually high. Which security issue is likely?
explanation: Check app permissions and data usage, and remove suspicious apps.

scenario: A mobile app won't open or crashes on launch. What should be tried first?
explanation: Then clear the app cache, reinstall or restart the device.

scenario: Why is rooting or jailbreaking a phone a security risk?
explanation: Rooted devices can run unapproved code and may lose updates and warranty support.

scenario: Windows shows a "low disk space" warning on C:. What should be done first?
explanation: Storage Sense can also clear temporary files automatically.

scenario: A program installed by a user keeps reinstalling itself after removal. What should be suspected?
explanation: Check startup items, scheduled tasks and services, and run a full scan.

scenario: A user can't open a document because no app is associated with its file type. What should be done?

options.text: Set or install a default app

explanation: File associations map extensions to apps.

scenario: Which tool can be used to remove an app that won't uninstall normally on Windows?
explanation: Some apps need a special cleanup tool; check Event Viewer for errors.

scenario: Windows displays "USB device not recognized" for a known-good flash drive. What should be tried first?

options.note: Checks the system drive, not USB.

explanation: Also check Device Manager for errors or power management settings.

scenario: A user's email client keeps asking for a password after it was changed. What should be done?
explanation: Credential Manager may store old passwords.

scenario: An app displays an error about a missing DLL file. What should be tried first?

options.text: Download the DLL from a random website

explanation: Reinstalling restores the app's required files.

scenario: A Windows PC restarts unexpectedly to install updates during work. How can this be prevented?

options.text: Set active hours or schedule restarts

explanation: Active hours tell Windows when not to restart.

scenario: After a malware cleanup, what should the technician do to reduce the chance of reinfection?
explanation: User education is the final step of malware removal.

scenario: A phone app requests access to contacts, location and SMS though it's only a flashlight. What should the user do?

options.text: Root the phone to control it
Move it to a different folder

explanation: Excessive permissions are a warning sign.

scenario: A user reports the cursor moves on its own and files open by themselves. What should be suspected?
explanation: Disconnect from the network and investigate immediately.

scenario: A user's system time is wrong after every restart. Which hardware issue might cause this?
explanation: Also check the time zone and time sync settings.

scenario: Which Windows feature boots with minimal drivers and services to troubleshoot problems?
explanation: Safe Mode with Networking also loads network drivers.

scenario: A user's apps are slow only when a nightly antivirus scan runs during work hours. What's a good fix?
explanation: Balance security with usability by scheduling scans.

scenario: Before replacing a laptop's motherboard, what should a technician use to protect components?

options.text: An ESD strap connected to ground
A magnetic screwdriver on the board

explanation: Use ESD mats and bags, and handle boards by the edges.

scenario: Which fire extinguisher type is safe for electrical fires?
explanation: Disconnect power if it's safe to do so.

scenario: Where should a technician find safe handling and disposal information for toner?
explanation: SDS documents describe hazards, handling, first aid and disposal.

scenario: How should old lithium-ion batteries be disposed of?

options.note: Still a fire hazard in trash.

explanation: Follow local regulations for batteries, CRTs and toner.

scenario: Which device keeps a server running briefly during a power outage so it can shut down safely?
explanation: UPS units also condition power.

scenario: What is the correct way to lift a heavy server?

options.text: Lift with your legs, back straight
Bend at the waist and lift

explanation: Get help or use a cart for heavy equipment.

scenario: Which backup type copies only files changed since the last backup of any type?

options.note: Changes since the last full backup.

explanation: Incremental backups are fast but restores need the full backup plus every incremental.

scenario: Which backup type copies all changes since the last FULL backup?

options.note: Since the last backup of any type.

explanation: Restores need the last full backup plus the latest differential.

scenario: What does the 3-2-1 backup rule recommend?

options.text: 3 copies, on 2 types of media, with 1 offsite

explanation: Testing restores regularly is just as important.

scenario: Before making a major change to a production server, what should usually be approved?

options.text: A change request and rollback plan
A new asset tag for the server
A backup of the server only

explanation: Change management includes purpose, scope, risk analysis, approval (often a change advisory board), testing and rollback.

scenario: What is a rollback plan?

options.text: Steps to undo a change if it fails
A list of new features to add

explanation: Always know how to return to the previous working state.

scenario: Which document records each IT support request and its resolution?

options.text: A ticket in the ticketing system
A sticky note on the monitor

explanation: Tickets capture the user, device, problem, steps taken, resolution and time spent.

scenario: Which best describes professional communication with a frustrated customer?

options.text: Listen, stay calm and avoid arguing
Take personal calls during the visit

explanation: Clarify the issue, set expectations and follow up.

scenario: A technician sees confidential documents on a customer's desk during a repair. What should they do?

options.text: Ignore them and keep the information private
Read them to understand the business
Take a photo for the ticket

explanation: Respect customer privacy and confidentiality at all times.

scenario: Which describes personally identifiable information (PII)?

options.text: Data that can identify a person

explanation: Protected health information (PHI) and payment card data (PCI DSS) have extra rules.

scenario: A technician finds illegal content on a work computer during a repair. What should they do?

options.text: Stop and follow the incident policy
Delete it and finish the repair
Copy it to a USB drive as proof
Ignore it and finish the repair

explanation: Maintain chain of custody and report to the appropriate person.

scenario: What is chain of custody?

options.text: A record of who handled evidence

explanation: It ensures evidence can be trusted later.

scenario: Which license type allows anyone to view and modify the source code?
explanation: Follow the license terms, such as attribution or sharing changes.

scenario: A user wants to install one software license on ten computers. What should the technician check?
explanation: Installing beyond the license is a violation.

scenario: Which script file type runs in Windows PowerShell?
explanation: Others: .bat (batch), .vbs (VBScript), .js (JavaScript), .sh (bash), .py (Python).

scenario: Which is a common, appropriate use of scripting for a help desk?
explanation: Scripts can automate backups, updates, restarts and gathering information.

scenario: What is a risk of running scripts from untrusted sources?

options.text: They always make PCs run faster

explanation: Review scripts before running them and test in a safe environment.

scenario: Which remote access tool is built into Windows for controlling a desktop remotely?
explanation: Other options include VNC, SSH, RMM tools, screen-sharing and VPNs.

scenario: Which tool lets an MSP monitor and manage many clients' computers from one console?
explanation: RMM tools patch, monitor and remotely support devices.

scenario: A user wants to paste customer records into a public AI chatbot to summarize them. What is the main concern?

options.text: The summary will be too short

explanation: Follow company policy; use approved AI tools and avoid sharing sensitive data.

scenario: An AI tool gives a confident answer with a made-up command. What is this called?
explanation: Verify AI output before using it, especially commands that change systems.

scenario: Which environmental control helps keep a server room safe for equipment?

options.text: Storing paper boxes next to racks

explanation: Low humidity increases ESD; high humidity causes condensation.

scenario: Why should cables in an office be managed with ties and covers?
explanation: Good cable management improves safety and airflow.
